purpose: Defines the internal Rust host crate's package metadata and requested dependency features.
behavior: Package metadata and lints inherit the workspace; publish=false marks this crate unavailable for direct registry publication at this pin.
This manifest requests Tokio rt-multi-thread, sync, time, io-util and net without explicitly requesting process; OS bindings are selected by cfg.
Serde, JSON and regex are development dependencies; sysinfo is a runtime dependency used for resource observation.
contracts: The listed Tokio features are this manifest's explicit requests, not a statement of Cargo's resolved feature union.
dependencies: native/omni/Cargo.toml supplies workspace versions and lint policy.
omni-proto defines the shared wire protocol.
failures_or_limits: Inherited versions and the resolved Cargo feature union cannot be established from this manifest alone.

purpose: Maps the Rust core to its builder, lifecycle, I/O and binding responsibilities.
behavior: README states run/spawn use a separate supervisor and that stopping targets a whole process tree.
Names Node bindings, the QA harness and Orchestra core/omni.ts as consumers.
Describes a three-OS workflow and points to the API contract and guarantees as the promise/evidence documents.
contracts: Documentation claims must be checked against implementation and actual CI receipts.

evidence.quote:
The Rust core of [Omni](../../README.md): it runs processes and terminals with the same behavior on Windows, macOS and
Linux. Callers build a `Command` (timeout, grace, cancel, pty and the rest) and call `run` or `spawn`. The crate never
creates a child itself: it asks the supervisor process to, so stopping a child ends its whole process tree.

- `bindings/node` (`hugr-omni-node`), the native addon behind the `hugr-omni` npm package.
- `qa` (the QA harness), which runs the same workloads through omni and through the standard library.
- In Orchestra, `packages/core/src/omni.ts` is the only module that imports `hugr-omni`.

## Build and test

The `omni` workflow (`.github/workflows/omni.yml`) runs `node scripts/ci.mjs`, which formats, lints with clippy and
runs `cargo test --workspace` on Linux, Windows and macOS. Tests are in `tests/` (`contract.rs`, `teeth.rs`) and next to
the modules.

The promises are in [docs/api-contract.md](../../docs/api-contract.md) and the per-OS evidence in
[GUARANTEES.md](../../GUARANTEES.md).

purpose: Builds immutable-per-launch requests from the public mutable Command options.
behavior: Builder stores program, argv, cwd, env mutations, timeout, grace, RSS cap, stdin and optional Windows verbatim tail without validating until launch.
run dispatches pipe or PTY by optional size; spawn delegates pipe validation; spawn_pty defaults to 80x24.
Run input data, per-stream output limits, cancellation, text decoding and pipe backpressure live in process Options rather than the wire request; Options has no input-size-limit field.
contracts: Verbatim tail is Windows-only, incompatible with argv and batch targets; validation is delegated.
Backpressure applies only to spawned pipe streams; run and terminals ignore it.
dependencies: src/process handles validation, launch, child handles and collection.
failures_or_limits: Builder comments promise 250 ms RSS sampling and whole-tree stopping; implementation resides below this file.

purpose: Defines the frozen public API export boundary.
behavior: Reexports Command, process child handles, stream/line readers, public value types and CancellationToken.
Keeps the command implementation private while exposing behavior types from their owning modules.
contracts: Names, signatures and docs are declared frozen except by lead decision recorded in PLAN.
dependencies: src/types.rs supplies public values; src/io and src/process supply behavior types.
failures_or_limits: No lifecycle or validation logic executes in this module.

purpose: Translates dynamic-language numeric options into Rust-safe values and configures the supervisor path.
behavior: millis accepts finite nonnegative numbers through u32 milliseconds and rounds fractional durations upward.
byte_limit requires a nonnegative integral value below 2^64 that fits usize; pty_side requires an integer 1..32767.
supervisor forwards configuration to client; embedded tests cover NaN, infinities, negatives, fractions and upper bounds.
contracts: Negative zero is accepted as zero; error text uses language-facing Infinity spellings.
Configured supervisor takes precedence and is constrained once a different supervisor starts.
failures_or_limits: Rust callers already have typed inputs; checks address TS/Python values. Embedded tests were read, not executed.

purpose: Owns one supervisor generation, serial request admission, bounded waiters and terminal failure.
behavior: Registers each waiter and writes/queues its frame under the same mutex; async requests receive watched deadlines and Stop adds grace to its budget.
Normal requests are rejected at 1024 pending while cleanup can use capacity through 8192; exhausting all capacity kills the generation.
Ready and synchronous round trips are bounded; death clears queues and deadlines, closes the channel, aborts workers, wakes all pending replies with Io and marks trees lost.
contracts: Request submission checks the host PID through home() before incrementing its request ID or mutating request state; forget() directly removes a local tree entry without its own home check.
No framing interleave and no reply-before-registration race; user wakeups occur outside the state lock.
dependencies: The platform Chan provides close and identity-checked termination; Unix identity checks are implemented in client/keeper.rs.
failures_or_limits: When required supervisor identity is unavailable, generation failure reports possible abandonment and the keeper declines to signal.
Distinct from abandonment, macOS keeper.rs checks the exit watch and start time then signals the PID; its documented check-to-signal interval can still permit PID reuse (lines 229–244).
